title: Powder Peaks: a ski-resort sim built part-time with Fable, Claude Ultracode & Sakana Fugu Ultra
author: bobo-the-merciful
selftext:
Hey everyone - sharing **Powder Peaks**, a ski resort management/tycoon game I've been building with a heavily AI-assisted workflow. Figured the *how* might be interesting to this sub.

The game is basically **RollerCoaster Tycoon meets a ski mountain**: you shape the terrain, place lifts and runs, manage the resort, and then watch skiers of different ability levels carve their own lines down the hill — with congestion, bottlenecks, crashes, and the emergent chaos of a busy ski day. Beginners stuck on runs that are too hard snowplow slowly and block the experts behind them, which creates a lot of the interesting problems to solve.

Video attached.

### The AI workflow

The interesting part for me has been treating AI agents less like a "one prompt = a game" button and more like a small dev team. Powder Peaks was built using:

- **Fable**
- **Claude Ultracode**
- **Sakana Fugu Ultra**
- **Beads**

The pattern was: break features into scoped tasks, point agents at a strict architecture spec with hard house rules (immutability, tests-first, strict file-ownership boundaries so agents don't stomp each other), and lean on CI gates to keep the output honest instead of letting it drift into slop. The constraints did more for quality than any single model did.

### Tech stack

- **Engine:** Phaser 4
- **Language:** TypeScript (strict)
- **Build:** Vite
- **Testing:** Vitest (unit, TDD-first) + Playwright (e2e)
- **Architecture:** pure-TypeScript simulation, fully decoupled from rendering
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG threaded through the whole sim → byte-identical saves, seed-replay, and a daily-challenge mode; enforced in CI by an AST lint (no `Math.random`/`Date.now` in sim code) plus a cross-platform state-hash check
- **Desktop:** browser-first, with the Steam build wrapped in Electron
- **Privacy:** zero network egress in the game build (fully offline, no tracking), also enforced in CI

The deterministic, renderer-decoupled sim turned out to be the thing that made AI-assisted dev work nicely - agents can hammer on isolated systems with fast, reliable tests instead of everything turning into spaghetti.

### Context

It's only been in active development for about **three weeks**, and I've done all of it **part-time** — alongside full-time consulting work and a young family at home. The agent-driven workflow is a big part of why that pace was even possible solo. Beads has been immense for just chucking ideas into the backlog.

Happy to go deep on any of it — agent coordination, the determinism setup, keeping AI output inside guardrails, whatever's useful.

If you want a ping when it releases: https://powder-peaks.com/

P.s. this post was written with the help of Sakanu Fugu Ultra in Codex CLI.
